newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ex-policeman convicted for communist crime.
newsitem.headline: Polish ex-policeman convicted for communist crime.

text.p: A Warsaw court jailed a former policeman for two years on Friday for his role in the fatal beating of an opposition student under communism.
The court said it could not pinpoint exactly who had beaten 18-year-old Grzegorz Przemyk in 1983 and sentenced Arkadiusz Denkiewicz for his role in the student's death.
"When Grzegorz Przemyk was being beaten, Denkiewicz appeared in the coridor and said to others: 'Beat him so as not to leave any traces,'" judge Barbara Sierpinska said, passing sentence.
Many Poles saw the the two-year trial and an earlier investigation into the case, reopened after the 1989 fall of communism, as attempting to rectify the crimes and injustices of the past.

Przemyk was picked up by a police patrol in Warsaw and taken to a police station where he was beaten up. He later died in hospital and his funeral turned into a massive protest againt the communist authorities.
Sierpinska said the court had acquitted a second policeman, Ireneusz Kosciuk, for lack of evidence.

The court handed down an 18-month suspended sentence to Kazimierz Otlowski, a former Interior Ministry official, for trying to destroy the files on the case in 1989 and 1990. A Warsaw court on Friday sentenced to a prison term a former communist policeman for involvement in a fatal beating of an opposition student, which horrified Poland in 1983.

The court said it could not pinpoint who exactly beat the 18-year old boy, son of Polish dissident poet Barbara Sadowska, and sentenced to two years in prison only for instigating to beat the student. Denkiewicz would have been sentenced to four years but the term was halved by the 1989 amnesty. The prosecutors demanded a 10-year jail term. @
